title: the README quickstart's st edit route loses a thread's objective at the next write, with a git recovery a fresh project cannot use
body:
Found by dc on 2026-09-24 driving the README quickstart for the 3.2.1 doc audit, in a scratch project on the pair at `4c687eaad`, with no intentd running.

Seen: the README teaches `intent st new`, then `intent st edit ST0001` "to record why it exists", then `intent ac new`. `st edit` opens `info.md` in the editor and returns, reading nothing back (`render.rs:1884-1885`). dc typed an objective into the file and ran `intent ac new ST0001 AC-01.1 --text ...`: it exited 0 with "warning: overwrote bytes that were not the store's render -- an edit to a generated file is gone: intent/st/ST0001/info.md", and the file and `intent st show` both read "objective: _(not yet written)_". The warning's remedy points at `git diff` / `git checkout`, and in a fresh project the file was never committed, so the text is unrecoverable. The in-essentials skill teaches the same route ("Its `## Objective` and `## Context` round-trip (`intent st edit <ID>`, ...)"). What works as built: `intent set ST0001 objective "..."`, or `intent sync --to-store` (or intentd's ingest) before the next write.

Why no carry reaches it, read by cc at HEAD: `st edit` realises the cover through `hydrate` (`facade.rs:6502`), which is not among `record_landed`'s callers, so a cover `st edit` realised has no recorded sha, is never "touched" (`ingest.rs:1300-1340`), and is carried by neither `intent sync --to-store` nor intentd's read-back; a cover last written by another verb (eg `st start`) has a recorded sha and is carried.

It is one family with 0556, 0568 and 0569: with no intentd running, the next Intent write destroys a hand edit to a thread's carried sections -- a CLI write with a warning (this issue), a hook's `sync --apply` after a pull, switch or rebase in silence (cc, measured the same day), and a doctor remedy that names only the discarding verb (0556).

Expected: no Intent write destroys a hand edit it could carry.

Disposition: hv's, asked on 2026-09-24, as part of that family, against the shipping-grade test of hv decision 33 (1). The README and getting-started teach `intent set` as the safe route, as built.


Scope in 3.2.1 (hv ruled the fix set in on 2026-09-24, relayed by vc; cc builds it), for the hooks' path in this family: `intent sync --apply`'s views step, which the post-merge, post-checkout and post-rewrite hooks run, leaves a view whose edit the store can carry and reports it as left, where today it rewrites it in silence. It uses the same carriable test as 0556's finding. This issue's own mechanism -- a cover `intent st edit` realised has no recorded sha, so the next CLI write overwrites it with a warning -- is not in this scope.

3.2.1 shipped the hooks' path at bcda3e7ea: `intent sync --apply` after a pull, a checkout or a rebase carries a hand edit to a cover's Objective or Context into the store. This issue's own route remains, after the stabilisation line: a cover `intent st edit` realised has no recorded sha, so the next CLI write renders over a hand edit to it with a warning; the README and getting-started teach `intent set`, as built.
